extracted.name: Skilled Worker visa
extracted.description: A Skilled Worker visa allows you to come to or stay in the UK to do an eligible job with an approved employer. It has replaced the Tier 2 (General) work visa.
eligibilityCriteria: work for a UK employer that’s been approved by the Home Office
have a ‘certificate of sponsorship’ (CoS) from your employer
do a job that’s on the list of eligible occupations
be paid a minimum salary - how much depends on the type of work you do and the date you got your CoS
You must be able to speak, read, write and understand English
extracted.applicationInstructions: You must apply online. You can apply for a visa up to 3 months before the day you are due to start work in the UK.

citations.validityPeriod: Your visa can last for up to 5 years before you need to extend it.
citations.isExtendable: You can apply to extend your visa as many times as you like as long as you still meet the eligibility requirements.

extracted.name: Standard Visitor visa
extracted.description: The Standard Visitor visa allows you to visit the UK for tourism, business, study (up to 6 months), and other permitted activities. You can usually stay for up to 6 months.
eligibilityCriteria: You must have a passport or travel document valid for the whole of your stay.
You must be able to show that you will leave the UK at the end of your visit.
You must be able to support yourself and your dependants during your trip (or have funding from someone else).
You must be able to pay for your return or onward journey (or have funding from someone else).
You must not live in the UK for extended periods through frequent or successive visits, or make the UK your main home.
extracted.applicationInstructions: You must apply online before you travel to the UK and attend an appointment at a visa application centre. The earliest you can apply is 3 months before you travel.

extracted.name: Student visa

extracted.name: Graduate visa
extracted.description: A Graduate visa allows you to stay in the UK for at least 18 months after successfully completing an eligible course with a Student visa. The duration is 2 years if you apply on or before 31 December 2026, or 18 months if you apply on or after 1 January 2027; PhD graduates get 3 years.
extracted.validityPeriod: 2 years if you apply on or before 31 December 2026; 18 months if you apply on or after 1 January 2027; 3 years for PhD or doctoral qualification
eligibilityCriteria: you’re in the UK
your current visa is a Student visa or Tier 4 (General) student visa
you studied a UK bachelor’s degree, postgraduate degree or other eligible course for a minimum period of time with your Student visa or Tier 4 (General) student visa
your education provider has told the Home Office you’ve successfully completed your course
extracted.applicationInstructions: You must apply online for a Graduate visa. You must be in the UK when you apply. You need to prove your identity and provide documents. You must apply before your Student visa or Tier 4 (General) student visa expires.

citations.processingTime: you’ll usually get a decision on your visa within 8 weeks
citations.fee.surcharge: pay the healthcare surcharge - this is usually £1,035 for each year you’ll be in the UK
citations.fee.years: 2 years if you apply on or before 31 December 2026
citations.validityPeriod: A Graduate visa lasts for: 2 years if you apply on or before 31 December 2026 18 months if you apply on or after 1 January 2027 If you have a PhD or other doctoral qualification, it will last for 3 years.
citations.isExtendable: You cannot extend your Graduate visa.
citations.eligibilityCriteria: You can apply for a Graduate visa if all of the following are true: you’re in the UK your current visa is a Student visa or Tier 4 (General) student visa you studied a UK bachelor’s degree, postgraduate degree or other eligible course for a minimum period of time with your Student visa or Tier 4 (General) student visa your education provider (such as your university or college) has told the Home Office you’ve successfully completed your course

extracted.name: Family visa
extracted.description: A visa to live with a family member in the UK for more than 6 months. It allows joining a spouse or partner, child, parent, or a relative who will provide long-term care.

feeComponents.label: Cost if joining your partner, parent or child

eligibilityCriteria: You and your partner must be 18 or over
Your partner must be a British or Irish citizen, settled in the UK, have pre-settled status, a Turkish Businessperson or Worker visa, protection status, or permission to stay as a stateless person
You must intend to live together permanently in the UK
You must prove your relationship (e.g., marriage, civil partnership, or living together for at least 2 years)
You must have a good knowledge of English
You must meet the financial requirements (minimum income of £29,000 per year unless exempt)
extracted.applicationInstructions: You must apply online from outside the UK. You'll need to prepare information and evidence to provide with your application.

citations.processingTime: If you apply outside the UK you’ll usually get a decision within 12 weeks.
citations.fee.application: Cost if joining your partner, parent or child £2,064
citations.fee.surcharge: For each adult (18 or older) it costs: £3,105 if you’re staying for 2 years and 9 months
citations.fee.years: You can stay in the UK for up to 2 years and 9 months.
citations.validityPeriod: You can stay in the UK for up to 2 years and 9 months.
citations.isExtendable: You can extend your visa more than once.
citations.eligibilityCriteria: To apply as a partner, you and your partner both need to be 18 or over. Your partner must also either: be a British or Irish citizen, have settled in the UK, be from the EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein and have pre-settled status, have a Turkish Businessperson visa or Turkish Worker visa, have protection status, have got permission to stay as a stateless person before you became their partner. You and your partner must intend to live together permanently in the UK after you apply. You must be able to prove one of the following: you’re in a civil partnership or marriage that’s recognised in the UK, you’ve been living together in a relationship for at least 2 years when you apply, you are a fiancé, fiancée or proposed civil partner and will marry or enter into a civil partnership in the UK within 6 months of arriving, you’ve been in a relationship for at least 2 years when you apply but you cannot live together. You also need to prove you: have a good knowledge of English, meet the financial requirements. If you apply for a family visa as a partner, you and your partner usually need to prove that your combined income is at least £29,000 a year.
citations.applicationInstructions: You must apply online from outside the UK.
